dispositions.reason: Step 4 takes the tenant from a client-supplied body field, which breaks AC-4's cross-organization isolation; the plan must look the invoice up with principal.orgId only and ignore any orgId in the body (and say which orgId the audit entry in step 8 uses: the principal's).

The SPEC has no parent/child organization model, so the 'on behalf of a child organization' sentence in step 4 is an unrequested addition; remove it from the plan together with the G1-1 fix (cross-organization refunds would need a SPEC change, not a plan one).
The AC-4 acceptance-mapping line should state that the test also posts with the other organization's id in the body and still gets 404, so the plan's own tenant-scoping fix is actually exercised.

The SPEC is silent on replaying a key with a different body and step 7 picks a behavior on its own; re-plan so the choice is stated as an explicit open question/assumption for a human to confirm (or switch to refusing a mismatch) instead of being decided silently.

GET /invoices/:id/refunds is in SPEC scope but no step or test covers it; add a planned test file or case for it (member allowed, other organization's invoice is 404, newest first) and list that file under Files.
The Risks section says the forward-only migration is noted in a README upgrade line that does not exist; step 11 and Files must add that line (or the risk text must stop claiming it).

Step 6 leaves the precedence of amount_invalid, reason_invalid and idempotency_key_invalid, and of a replay with a malformed amount, to the builder; fix one total order of checks in the plan since the build needs it to be deterministic.

Step 10 uses req.headers in the handler snippet while also saying handlers receive headers; make the snippet consistent (pass the idempotency header through the new headers parameter) so the build can carry it out as written.

The Concurrency risk says simultaneous refunds 'cannot' both pass, which holds only for one server process on the data file; reword it to state the single-process limit instead of an unconditional guarantee.

The SPEC asks for an audit entry for every recorded refund (AC-6) and says nothing about logging refused attempts; adding logging or metrics for refusals would be a speculative addition outside scope.
